# HeliCam C4 polarity — Python exploration log

Direct Python control of the camera and PulseBlaster, 2026-08-16. MATLAB was not
running and is not involved at any point in these measurements.

**Result in one line:** the camera's demodulation weight function is the exact negative of
Eq. 5.54, measured directly, stable across 15 acquisitions, and independent of MATLAB, of the
sequence period defect, and of optical power.

Scripts live in the session scratchpad (`hcpb.py` plus `stage0.py` … `stage6.py`); the
per-stage arrays are in `stages/`.

---

## Control layer

| | |
| --- | --- |
| PulseBlaster | `spinapi64.dll` via `ctypes`, 500 MHz core clock, opcodes from `pulseblaster.h` |
| Camera | `harvesters` 1.4.3 + `genicam` 1.5.1 through the Diaphus GenTL producer |
| Camera identity | `DiaphusTL_DEV_192.168.0.68`, serial 145118, firmware 1.11.0, 542 × 512 |

**Safety contract:** every script parks the PulseBlaster with *all outputs low* on exit,
including on exception. This deliberately differs from MATLAB, which parks the board with
GreenAOM **high** after a run.

**Sequence generation** is done here rather than by `PBFunctionPool`, so one loop iteration is
exactly 4Q. The laser spans are shifted earlier by the 200 ns AOM compensation and wrap
modulo the period, which avoids the period stretch described in Stage 6.

---

## Stage 0 — access baseline

*Tried:* software unit-test of the sequence generator; open PulseBlaster, park low, close;
open camera, read identity, close. Nothing energized.

*Result:* generator emits exactly 200000 ns for every laser placement, CamRef rises at
0/50/100/150 µs. PulseBlaster: 1 board, spinapi 20171214. Camera identity as above.

## Stage 1 — offset baseline, laser never fired

*Tried:* (a) arm the camera with **no** reference train at all; (b) CamRef train only, laser
channel held low.

*Result:*

- (a) `TimeoutException` after 4.3 s — confirms the burst really is gated by the external
  CamRef edges, and that a starved burst returns nothing rather than partial data.
- (b) offset image: **I = 517.86, Q = 530.65**. Frame-to-frame spread of mean(I) was
  516.4 / 518.2 / 518.2 / 518.6.

The I offset matches the ~517 pedestal recorded in `hc_DarkRef`'s docstring and the 518.5 of
the stored Aug-12 dark. The Q offset of 530.65 matches that file's stored `rawsignal` of
−531.3, which independently confirms the Aug-12 MATLAB convention was `rawsignal = -mean(Q)`
and that the Aug-14 files (`rawsignal` ≈ +468, positive) were written with the opposite sign.

## Stage 2 — reproduce the inversion with MATLAB out of the loop

*Tried:* dark and lit acquired back to back in one session, laser through Q1+Q2 (what
`hc_Image` currently does), uniform 4 × 50 µs period, raw components decoded here.

*Result:*

| | mean | beam centre | corners |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I dark | 517.98 | 517.62 | 514.20 |
| I lit | 493.97 | 414.63 | 511.92 |
| **I lit − dark** | −24.01 | **−102.99** | −2.28 |
| **Q lit − dark** | −24.51 | **−103.06** | −2.95 |

97.8 % of dI pixels and 98.5 % of dQ pixels negative; correlation dI vs dQ = 0.9931, as
expected when the laser spans Q1 and Q2 so both components see the same light.

![Reference as measured, the offset image, the offset-corrected reference, and the same with an inverted grey scale](data:image/png;base64,)

Panel c is a minus b per pixel; panel d is panel c with only the lookup table reversed, no
arithmetic, and shows the bright spot and dark shadow actually in front of the sensor.

The inversion is therefore **not** a MATLAB sign convention, **not** the `rawsignal` sign
confusion, and **not** the non-uniform period.

## Stage 3 — four-placement table

*Tried:* laser confined to one quarter at a time, dark taken before and after.

| laser in | dI centre | dQ centre | channel | isolation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| q1 | **−101.68** | +0.52 | −I | 195× |
| q2 | −0.04 | **−102.39** | −Q | 2925× |
| q3 | **+103.16** | +0.44 | +I | 236× |
| q4 | +0.15 | **+103.91** | +Q | 693× |

Dark drift across the whole run: dI −0.04, dQ +0.20.

*Result:* the pattern is `q1→−I, q2→−Q, q3→+I, q4→+Q` — the exact negation of Eq. 5.54. The
near-perfect channel isolation rules out any fractional-quarter phase error: a non-integer
offset would leak substantially into both channels, and it does not. This is either a global
polarity inversion or a rotation of the quarter grid by exactly two, which are
indistinguishable.

## Stage 4 — stability

*Tried:* laser fixed in q1. (A) 8 consecutive acquisitions, same session and configuration;
(B) 4 acquisitions with `configure()` re-run in between; (C) 3 acquisitions with the camera
fully disconnected and reopened in between.

| group | dI mean | sd | dQ mean | sd | sign flips |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | −101.97 | 0.15 | +0.31 | 0.14 | 0 |
| B | −101.99 | 0.18 | +0.24 | 0.06 | 0 |
| C | −101.82 | 0.24 | +0.22 | 0.05 | 0 |

*Result:* across all 15 runs dI stayed negative with a total range of
[−102.25, −101.64] — 0.6 % spread. No hopping between the four possible states, not even
across a full device close and reopen. **The effect is deterministic and can safely be
calibrated away.** It also rules out a quarter-counter phase that lands randomly at the start
of each acquisition.

## Stage 5 — demodulation weight function, measured directly

*Tried:* a 4 µs laser pulse stepped in 2.5 µs increments across the full 200 µs period, 80
points, recording beam-centre dI and dQ at each.

| quarter | measured dI | measured dQ | Eq. 5.54 wants |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| q1 | **−7.78** | +0.06 | I = +1 |
| q2 | +0.07 | **−7.59** | Q = +1 |
| q3 | **+7.94** | +0.30 | I = −1 |
| q4 | +0.09 | **+8.08** | Q = −1 |

Dark drift across the sweep: +0.18.

![Measured dI and dQ versus laser pulse position across one lock-in period, against the weights expected from Eq. 5.54](data:image/png;base64,)

*Result:* the measured weight is the negative of the documented one in all four quarters. Two
further facts fall out of the sweep, neither of which was accessible before:

- **The quarter boundaries coincide with our trigger edges.** The sign transition happens
  between 47.5 µs and 52.5 µs for the 50 µs edge, and likewise at every other edge. There is
  no phase offset to correct.
- **The dead zone is visible and matches Eq. 5.63.** The response falls to ~0.7–1.2 (from a
  full ~8.7) in the last 2.5 µs before each trigger edge, and returns to full within 2.5 µs
  after it. That is the 4.3 µs sensor-busy window predicted by
  t_busy = 1/(4 · 5208.33 · 1.05) = 45.7 µs of a 50 µs quarter, and it independently confirms
  that the exposure begins right after the trigger, as §5.2.2 and §5.2.5 describe.

## Stage 6 — does the non-uniform period matter?

`PBFunctionPool` stretches the loop to 4Q + 1200 ns: `dummy1`'s second marker pulse starts at
4Q and runs 1000 ns beyond it, and `ApplyDelays`' 200 ns AOM compensation adds another 200 ns
because [PBFunctionPool.m:87](../PBFunctionPool.m#L87) shifts the earliest event to zero. Three
quarters are therefore 50.0 µs and the fourth is 51.2 µs.

*Tried:* the same laser placement (q1) measured with my uniform generator and with an exact
replica of the MATLAB sequence including the marker channel.

| sequence | period | dI centre | dQ centre |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| uniform | 200000 ns | −101.67 | +0.34 |
| MATLAB replica | 201200 ns | −101.39 | +0.41 |

*Result:* a 0.3 % difference, inside the 0.15–0.24 run-to-run noise of Stage 4. The period
defect is real and worth fixing for cleanliness, but it is **not** connected to the polarity
problem. It also never starves the burst, because 51.2 µs still exceeds the 45.7 µs busy time.

---

## What is now established

1. The demodulation weight is the exact negative of Eq. 5.54 in all four quarters.
2. Quarter boundaries align with our trigger edges; there is no fractional phase error.
3. The sensor-busy dead zone is where the manual says it is, ~4.3 µs at the end of each quarter.
4. The effect is deterministic and stable to 0.6 % over 15 acquisitions, surviving
   reconfiguration and reconnection.
5. It is independent of MATLAB, of the `rawsignal` sign confusion, of the non-uniform period,
   and (from the earlier power series) of optical power.

## What remains unresolved

The mechanism. A global polarity inversion of the decoded output and a rotation of the α/β/γ/δ
assignment by exactly two quarters produce identical data, and Stage 5 confirms they cannot be
separated by any measurement on our side — the boundaries and dead zones sit in the same places
under both. Only Heliotis can say which it is.

For doing physics it does not matter: both take the same correction, negate both components,
and Stage 4 shows that correction is safe to apply.

## Loose ends found along the way

- `rawsignal`'s sign convention changed between the Aug-12 and Aug-14 MATLAB runs (Stage 1).
  Every saved `.h5` should be checked against its date before use, and the stored dark
  reference's Q half is in the opposite convention from the Aug-14 files.
- `hc_Image.m`'s docstring and its `% laser fills Q1` comment describe none of the three
  laser placements the file has actually had.
- The `dummy1` period marker lengthens every sequence by its own `DT` (Stage 6).
